content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, T4C).**

The only term/termination provision is paragraph 4(a)–(b) (p0016). Key issues:

1. **No AP convenience right during the committed term** — "Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term," and the Agreement auto-renews into successive 1-year terms, so AP is locked in indefinitely absent breach.
2. **Kubient gets a mid-term walk-away** — the "for any reason … upon ninety (90) days written notice" right after the Initial Term operates mid-renewal-term, not just at term end.
3. **Effective early-termination penalty and no refund** — Kubient "shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates," with no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.

Redline (validated ok:true) reaches the preferred position with a single replacement: AP may terminate for convenience, in whole or in part, on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid fees and no penalty; Kubient may not terminate for convenience mid-term but may exit effective at the end of the then-current Term on 90 days' notice; Kubient's fee entitlement is trimmed to fees generated through the effective date. The comment offers the 60-day fallback.
